<l0/> groups related items under a label. <l1/> draws a divider. Both accept `render` and `className`, and carry `context-menu-group` and `context-menu-separator` as their `data-slot`.
A context menu is a shortcut. Make every action in it reachable some other way too, such as a visible button or a dropdown menu, since many people never right click or long press.
A disabled <l0/> gives the area back to the browser’s own menu. Disabled items stay visible but are skipped by the keyboard.
Browsers also fire the context menu event for Shift F10 and the Menu key on a focused element, so a focusable element inside the trigger lets keyboard users open it.
Built on the Base UI context menu. Every part accepts the props of the primitive it wraps, and a function `className` that receives the part’s state.
